study.question: Does auxiliary-supervised event selection help click prediction after harmful coefficient-mass changes are removed, and does click rewriting of donor gates help or interfere?
study.hypothesis: The latest local factorial shows redistribution-only click gating at AUC 0.6633488027 versus full 0.6626801586, scale-only 0.6617903610 and none 0.6617449728. The gain over full concentrates in histories >64 (0.6659400 versus 0.6648231); short-history improvement is much smaller and empty-history performance is lower. Earlier full-gate auxiliary donors did not beat self donors: detached difference -0.0001077056 and live difference -0.0000560718. Provisional mechanism: coefficient-mass interference may have obscured complementary auxiliary event allocation. Under mass preservation, a donor protected from click gradients may supply a different useful ordering; allowing click to rewrite it may erase that distinction. This is a consequential follow-up of an unsuccessful branch, not a claim that the old failure was caused by mass changes.

nearest_work.difference: Archived exact-version primary text lines 250-277 motivates target-conditioned weighted pooling and retention of interest intensity. Inherit local activation, but preserve learned signed-score L1 mass while varying supervision of an additional gate. This is not unit softmax normalization, exact original DIN reproduction or a priority claim.

Pinned benchmark source lines 236-313 uses hub aggregation and global-to-local affine gated broadcasts. Here only existing scalar event-gate rows communicate through a fixed mean donor before click L1-preserving normalization; no hubs, token updates or imported implementation. Original INFNet full paper remains unaudited.

Cached primary benchmark section 2.3 describes stacked and layer-wise unified interaction. This suite isolates task supervision in a local event selector instead of reproducing one of those whole architectures.

Same fixed 0.5 auxiliary gate-logit donor and detach intervention, now under the independently motivated redistribution-only click operator. Existing full-gate four-cell results remain historical controls; interaction comparisons across rounds are secondary.

Direct parent source hash verified. Keep its mass-preserving operator and all parameter construction; reopen only donor identity and donor backward ownership. Include a byte-identical source copy as the contemporaneous self/live control.

study.proposed_difference: Complete the donor identity (mean of all three auxiliary gate rows versus click row) by donor gradient (detached versus live) factorial under click redistribution-only. For valid event e, z*_click=z_click+0.5*d; g=1+tanh(z*); r_e=s_e*g_e*sum|s|/sum|s*g|, with inherited zero-mass fallback. Other task gates and readouts stay unchanged. Detach applies only to d, not to base scores, normalizers, primary z, or auxiliary losses. All arms start at the same zero-gate function. No added parameters, losses, data or RNG draws.
predictions: Primary directional prediction: mass-preserving auxiliary/detached exceeds matched self/detached click AUC. Auxiliary/live versus self/live tests whether the direction survives click gradient coupling. Neither contrast is claimed positive before host evaluation.

If protecting auxiliary specialization matters, auxiliary/detached should beat auxiliary/live beyond the corresponding self detached/live change. Report this difference-in-differences even if negative.

At a fixed model state live/detached have identical forward outputs. The click-loss direct gradient into auxiliary donor rows is zero only in the detached arm; live generally supplies nonzero gradients on a heterogeneous nondegenerate batch.

For fixed base scores, click coefficient L1 mass is conserved for every donor choice, padding contributes zero, and empty-history pooling/evidence remain exactly zero before learned downstream paths. Whole-model empty-history predictions may change after training through shared learning.

Long-history slices 17-64 and >64 are predeclared diagnostics; all four task AUC/Logloss, auxiliary mean AUC, parameters, wall/GPU seconds, peak memory, throughput and p50/p95 batch latency must be reported. Primary selection remains full-population click AUC.
falsifiers: If auxiliary/detached does not beat self/detached and auxiliary/live does not beat self/live, complementary auxiliary gate transfer remains unsupported after mass control; retain the incumbent rather than relabeling a null result as success.
If both donor types respond similarly to detach/live, the protected-specialization explanation is unsupported even if one arm improves click AUC.

If benefits appear only with live donor gradients, auxiliary-supervised complementary information cannot be separated from click using extra update paths without a follow-up supervision replacement control.
A failed mass, padding, initialization, finite-output or gradient-ownership check invalidates mechanistic interpretation. Execution failure is not scientific falsification.
One favorable fixed-seed result is provisional. A tiny lead without paired-seed/user-cluster uncertainty cannot establish repeated support, and no novelty claim is made.
alternative_explanations: Donor rows all use the same event features, so this changes supervision/optimization, not forward expressive capacity.
Self donor scales the click gate logit by 1.5; auxiliary donor combines rows. Effective gradient scales differ and live/detached self controls do not eliminate all optimization explanations.
Shared context, dense gradient clipping and BatchNorm remain indirect coupling paths.
A single fixed training seed and repeated use of validation cannot establish generalization or mechanism significance.
The latest normalization gain can reflect optimization geometry, BF16 rounding, signed-value cancellation or one-pass calibration rather than a forward allocation mechanism alone.

Earlier negative branches included live auxiliary trunks, shared item-gradient paths, partial item sharing and pooled representation transfer; capacity-only and task-independent evidence also explained portions of gains. These outcomes argue against assuming all auxiliary information is useful.

Historical cart/fav/buy masks may overlap and the labels match user/category/brand over 24h; rare-task gate estimates and offline action maturity can limit transfer. No advertisement-specific conversion interpretation is assumed.
Different task gate rows are linear functions of the same inputs; a useful donor can be regularization or training dynamics rather than a new representation family.

trajectory_review.scope: All 49 allowed trial-index records reviewed, including baseline and negative/abandoned branches. No execution failures in the supplied index; previous_runtime_error is null.
observations: Primary selector ownership and item-gradient isolation beat joint supervision locally; reducing auxiliary loss and partial gradient sharing did not recover the best click result.
Private learned auxiliary items did not improve click over fixed tables; no general auxiliary capacity benefit established.
Pooled learned auxiliary transfer and partial field sharing underperformed their relevant parents.
Target-matched evidence and event-level gates helped; feedback identity increments were small, so identity-specific complementarity remains weakly supported.
Round10 auxiliary donors failed to beat self donors; round11 redistribution-only improved click versus full, scale and none. These are distinct observations, not retroactive confirmation of transfer.
trajectory_review.maturity: Single-seed controlled observations, provisional explanations; no repeated mechanism support and no new measured candidate outcome.
